agenda: Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is to secure a strong Council condemnation of the Palmyra attack against U.S. and Syrian personnel, reinforce implementation of resolution 2799, and press Syria and all Member States to sustain counter-ISIL and counter-terrorism cooperation without authorizing new mandates. The main difficulty will be balancing a robust U.S. priority on counterterrorism and self-defence with Russia and China’s sensitivity to sovereignty, unilateral military action, and any language they may read as endorsing U.S. strikes. We also expect some members to seek additional humanitarian and human-rights safeguards and to narrow references to specific recent attacks.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft's strong condemnation of the recent terrorist attacks and its focus on full implementation of the 1267 regime. We ask that OP5 explicitly require the consent of and close coordination with the Syrian Arab Republic, that a preambular reference be added to the Syrian-owned and Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254 (2015) and conditions conducive to terrorism, and that the Secretary-General's reporting in OP8 cover the Sahel and Lake Chad Basin. With these adjustments, Algeria is prepared to support the text.
messages.China: China supports the Council’s clear condemnation of the recent terrorist attacks and the draft’s counter-terrorism thrust. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text by naming ETIM/TIP, by ensuring that counter-terrorism cooperation fully respects the sovereignty and consent of the host State, and by avoiding any impression that the Global Coalition is being endorsed. China also believes that any further adjustment of Syria-related sanctions must be carefully assessed against the counter-terrorism situation and the concerns of all parties.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft and welcomes its strong condemnation of recent attacks and its focus on accountability, including for sexual and gender-based violence. We ask for targeted additions to safeguard humanitarian access, ensure that online counter-terrorism measures respect freedom of expression and privacy, and require reporting on compliance with international law and protection of civilians. These changes would strengthen the text’s consistency with Denmark’s human-rights-based approach to counter-terrorism.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for its penholdership and supports the resolution’s firm condemnation of the Palmyra, Bondi Beach and Maiduguri attacks. We would like the text to anchor more explicitly the accountability owed to survivors of Da’esh’s sexual and gender-based violence, including Yazidis and other minorities, and to include a clear safeguard that counter-terrorism measures do not impede impartial humanitarian action. With these adjustments, France is ready to support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece broadly supports the draft and welcomes its strong condemnation of the Palmyra, Bondi Beach and Maiduguri attacks. We ask the penholder to add operative safeguards in OP6 so that counterterrorism cooperation, including on Internet and social media, is expressly in full compliance with international law and human rights, including freedom of expression and privacy. We would also add a reference to non-refoulement in OP3 in the context of border security. With these adjustments, Greece can support the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as circulated. It reflects our priorities of condemning terrorism in all its forms, upholding sovereignty and international law, protecting civilians, and ensuring accountability. We encourage the penholder to retain the balanced references to international humanitarian law, human rights law and refugee law.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the United States for the draft and supports its overall thrust. We request explicit language against Islamophobia and religious intolerance, and a clear safeguard that counter-terrorism efforts in Syria, including those of the Global Coalition, are undertaken in coordination with and with the consent of the Syrian Arab Republic and fully respect its sovereignty. We also ask for a comprehensive approach addressing conditions conducive to terrorism through education, development and dialogue among civilizations.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for the balanced draft and can support it. We ask that operative obligations expressly incorporate the full range of international law, and that cooperation include capacity-building and maritime and port security assistance for developing States. We would also welcome a slightly broader reporting clause covering humanitarian impact and capacity needs. Panama remains ready to work constructively to adopt a strong consensus text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft and thanks the United States for its leadership. We propose adding a reference to virtual assets and other new payment methods in OP6 to reflect evolving terrorist financing risks, and a brief reference to victim and survivor support in OP7. We are flexible on exact placement and remain ready to work with the penholder.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation can support the draft, but it needs balanced amendments. We cannot accept welcoming the US-led Global Coalition, whose operations in Syria lack the consent of the Syrian Government; OP5 must take note of efforts by States and regional organizations in coordination with Damascus. We also ask that references to 'sexual and gender-based violence' be replaced by 'sexual violence', and that the reporting in OP8 not single out Syria but cover implementation by all Member States in full respect for sovereignty.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the penholder's draft and supports its adoption, given the gravity of the Palmyra, Bondi Beach and Maiduguri attacks and the need for full implementation of the 1267 regime. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 with FATF/AML-CFT technical assistance for developing countries, particularly in Africa, and OP5 by recognizing African Union, ECOWAS, MNJTF and Accra Initiative efforts and calling for predictable and sustainable financing for African-led counter-terrorism. We would also support a small addition in OP6 on education, youth engagement and socio-economic development as part of addressing conditions conducive to terrorism. These changes would strengthen consensus and reflect African priorities.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the draft’s condemnation and its emphasis on accountability, including for sexual and gender-based violence, and can join consensus. We ask the penholder to add explicit child-protection language: children associated with terrorist groups must be treated primarily as victims, with access to rehabilitation, reintegration and repatriation where appropriate. We also suggest a modest safeguard in OP6 that measures on the Internet and social media comply with international law, including freedom of expression and privacy.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft’s strong condemnation of terrorism and its Chapter VII approach. We ask that Al-Shabaab be explicitly named in the operative demands, given the severe and ongoing threat it poses in Somalia and the wider Horn of Africa. We also seek language on predictable support for African Union-led peace support operations and capacity-building for affected States, and clarification that counterterrorism cooperation respects host-State consent and sovereignty.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the penholder’s draft and its focus on ISIL/Da’esh, Al-Qaida and accountability. We would like targeted additions to OP6 and OP7 to protect freedom of expression and privacy online and to support survivors, including survivors of sexual and gender-based violence. We also suggest a new operative paragraph making clear that counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law and not impede humanitarian access or protection of civilians. We are ready to work with the penholder and other members to finalise the text.

replies.Algeria: accepted: OP5 consent language, 2254 preambular language, and broader Sahel/Lake Chad reporting included.
replies.China: accepted: ETIM/TIP named, non-politicization language added, OP5 neutralized, and sanctions-assessment preambular paragraph included.
replies.Denmark: accepted: humanitarian access, privacy/expression safeguards, and compliance reporting included.
replies.France: accepted: minority SGBV references, survivor access, and humanitarian-action safeguard included.
replies.Greece: accepted: OP6 international-law safeguards and OP3 non-refoulement language included.
replies.Pakistan: accepted: Islamophobia reference, host-State consent, and conditions-conducive language included.
replies.Panama: accepted: international-law language, capacity-building, and humanitarian-impact reporting included.
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: virtual-assets language and victim/survivor support included.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP5 red line and OP8 reporting language accommodated; SGBV retained but explicitly includes sexual violence.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: FATF assistance, African partners, financing language, and education/youth provisions included.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: child-protection preambular and operative language plus OP6 safeguards included.
replies.Somalia: partially accepted: Al-Shabaab named and host-State consent included; AU support framed with Security Council authorization and voluntary financing.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: OP6 online safeguards, OP7 survivor support, and new international-law/humanitarian paragraph included.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates core concerns across the Council by naming ETIM/TIP and Al-Shabaab, removing explicit endorsement of the Global Coalition in favor of neutral language with host-State consent, and broadening reporting and humanitarian/human-rights safeguards. It retains US priorities on condemning the Palmyra attack, accountability including SGBV, and full implementation of the 1267 regime.

Pakistan.change: Insert “Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)” after “Boko Haram” in the list of terrorist groups.
Insert “without double standards or politicization” after “fully implement their obligations under the relevant Security Council resolutions”.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals in revision 1, including the consent and coordination language in OP5, the 2254 preambular reference, and the broader Sahel/Lake Chad reporting in OP8. The current text reflects a balanced approach that upholds Syrian sovereignty, African-led counter-terrorism efforts and international law. Algeria supports the draft as it stands and looks forward to its adoption.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for taking on board its proposals on ETIM/TIP, non-politicization, respect for sovereignty and the need for a comprehensive assessment before any further Syria-related sanctions adjustment. The current text reflects these concerns in a balanced manner. China supports the draft and encourages the Council to adopt it by consensus.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the current revised text and has no further requests. The revisions reflect key Danish priorities on humanitarian access, human rights safeguards, and compliance reporting. We encourage all members to unite behind the text and ensure its full implementation.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for the revised text and welcomes that our proposals on conflict-related sexual violence, access to justice for survivors, and the humanitarian safeguard are reflected. We support the text as it stands and believe it should be put to the vote without delay. We stress that its implementation must remain fully consistent with international law, including human rights and humanitarian law, and that the Council will hold the Syrian authorities to the expectations recalled in resolution 2799 (2025).
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the incorporation of the international-law safeguards in OP6 and the non-refoulement language in OP3. The text now strikes an appropriate balance between robust counter-terrorism action and respect for international law, including human rights and refugee law. Greece supports the draft as presented and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the current text and will vote in favour. We welcome the reaffirmation of international law, sovereignty, protection of civilians, and the emphasis on capacity-building for developing countries, particularly in Africa. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and proceed to a vote.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the revised draft and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier concerns on Islamophobia, host-State consent and conditions conducive to terrorism. We request two final refinements: explicitly name TTP among the terrorist groups in OP2, given the severe threat it poses to Pakistan and the region, and make the no-double-standards/no-politicization principle in OP3 apply to all Member States, not only Syria in OP4. With these changes, Pakistan is ready to support the resolution.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder for incorporating our previous proposals on international law, capacity-building, and reporting on humanitarian impact and capacity-building needs. The current text is balanced and consistent with Panama’s commitment to counter-terrorism, sovereignty and international law, including international humanitarian, human rights and refugee law. We therefore support the draft as it stands and encourage the Council to send a unified message.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on virtual assets and victim and survivor support. We support the current text and call on the Council to speak with one voice against terrorism, including ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida and their affiliated groups. We encourage full implementation consistent with international law and remain ready to support consensus.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation thanks the penholder for accommodating our core concerns in OP5 and OP8. The current text preserves Syrian sovereignty, removes the politicized reference to the Global Coalition, and bases reporting on information from Member States and the 1267 Monitoring Team. We can support the draft as it stands; our preference for 'sexual violence' terminology in PP9 and OP7 is noted but is not a blocker.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the revised draft, which reflects our priorities on African-led counter-terrorism cooperation, predictable financing, FATF-related capacity-building, and education and youth engagement. We also appreciate the strong provisions on protection of civilians, children associated with terrorist groups, and sexual and gender-based violence. We support the text as it stands and will vote in favour, while encouraging full implementation and reporting on humanitarian impact and capacity-building needs.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text as a balanced and human-rights-compliant basis for Council action. We welcome that our child-protection, survivor-accountability and OP6 safeguards were incorporated, and we encourage all Member States to implement the resolution in full conformity with international law, including IHL, IHRL and refugee law. We are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised text and welcomes the inclusion of Al-Shabaab, host-State consent, and enhanced support for African-led counter-terrorism and AU-led peace support operations. We request that OP8 explicitly include Al-Shabaab and the Horn of Africa, including Somalia, in the Secretary-General's reporting scope. With that modest addition, Somalia can support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the revised text and the incorporation of our proposed safeguards on internet measures, survivor support, and the international-law and humanitarian paragraph. The draft strikes the right balance between strong counter-terrorism action and the protection of human rights and humanitarian access, and we can support it as it stands. We encourage the Council to show unity and move swiftly to adoption.

replies.Pakistan: accepted: both refinements incorporated in OP2 and OP3
replies.Somalia: accepted: OP8 amended to include Al-Shabaab, Horn of Africa and Somalia

steps.summary: The United States accepted Pakistan's request to name TTP in OP2 and to extend the no-double-standards principle to all Member States in OP3, reinforcing full implementation of Council obligations. We also accepted Somalia's OP8 request so reporting covers Al-Shabaab and the Horn of Africa, including Somalia. The revised text retains U.S. priorities and is expected to be adopted by consensus.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria had already signalled support in the last negotiation round and requested no changes; the draft aligns with its anti-terrorism priorities, emphasis on international law, African capacity-building, and Syrian sovereignty. Voting in favour is consistent with its record on this agenda item.
reasons.China: China supports the draft’s balanced counter-terrorism focus, including explicit listing of ETIM/TIP and calls against double standards, and made no amendment requests in negotiations. No pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark’s last position was support with no requested changes, and the draft reflects Danish priorities on international law, humanitarian access, accountability, and African capacity-building. Voting in favour is consistent with Denmark’s prior votes on this agenda item and its alliance posture.
reasons.France: France supports the US-drafted resolution, which aligns with its priorities on countering ISIL/Al-Qaida, accountability, international law, and African counter-terrorism capacity. No pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Greece: Greece had already signalled support for the draft, which aligns with its firm condemnation of terrorism, support for international law and humanitarian safeguards, and backing for Syria and Africa-related counter-terrorism cooperation. No red lines required a negative vote or abstention.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported previous Council resolutions on this agenda item and had indicated support in the last negotiation round. The draft aligns with Guyana’s emphasis on international law, humanitarian safeguards, sovereignty, and support for African-led counter-terrorism capacity.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan had requested the explicit listing of TTP and language against double standards and politicization, both of which the penholder accepted. The revised text aligns with Pakistan’s core counter-terrorism priorities, so it votes in favour.
reasons.Panama: Panama has consistently supported this agenda item and had no outstanding changes; the text aligns with its priorities on international law, sovereignty, and maritime and port security, so it votes in favour with a brief explanation.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported Security Council counter-terrorism resolutions, and this draft aligns with its support for international cooperation against ISIL/Al-Qaida, accountability, and protection of civilians. It raised no concerns in negotiations and would not need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft aligns with Russia's counter-terrorism priorities, including respect for sovereignty, Syrian coordination, and African capacity-building. With no outstanding requests and broad consensus, Russia votes in favour without taking the floor before the vote.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone consistently supports US-led counter-terrorism resolutions and its key priorities, especially African capacity-building, international law, SGBV accountability and FATF standards, are reflected. It would vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia had already signalled support and the text contains its key priorities on international law, humanitarian access, child protection and SGBV accountability. Voting in favour is consistent with its prior votes on this agenda item and its Council record.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia had supported the draft with changes, and its key OP8 amendment was accepted; voting in favour advances its core counter-terrorism interest in recognition of Al-Shabaab and support for Somalia and African-led efforts.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft aligns with the UK’s counter-terrorism priorities, support for international law and human rights safeguards, and strong condemnation of recent attacks. The UK has no substantive objections and will support the broad consensus in favour.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and sponsor, and the draft advances its counter-terrorism priorities, including accountability for the Palmyra attack and support for Syrian cooperation under Resolution 2799. Voting in favour is consistent with its record and interests.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it responds to the continuing and grave threat posed by ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida and their affiliated groups, including in Syria and across Africa, and because it condemns in the strongest terms the recent terrorist attacks, including in Palmyra, Bondi Beach and Maiduguri. Algeria welcomes the text’s reaffirmation that counter-terrorism measures must be consistent with international law, including the Charter, human rights law, refugee law and humanitarian law, and that they must not impede impartial humanitarian action. We also underscore the importance of respecting the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of all Member States, and of ensuring that counter-terrorism is not associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group. Algeria firmly supports African-led counter-terrorism efforts and capacity-building for developing countries, including in the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and Horn of Africa, and stresses that such efforts should be undertaken in full respect for the sovereignty of the States concerned and, where applicable, with their consent. We further emphasize that the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions regime must preserve its integrity and remain Member State-driven, without politicization or double standards. Algeria will continue to support constructive international cooperation against terrorism while upholding the principles of the Charter and the legitimate aspirations of all peoples to peace, stability and development.
before.Denmark: Denmark condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Palmyra and all recent terrorist attacks, including those in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri, and extends its condolences to the victims’ families. Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the text’s clear reaffirmation that counter-terrorism measures must be consistent with international law, including human rights law, refugee law and international humanitarian law, and that impartial humanitarian action must not be impeded. We particularly value the attention given to accountability for sexual and gender-based violence, the treatment of children associated with terrorist groups as victims, support for survivors, and the call for strengthened, predictable support for African-led counter-terrorism efforts and affected states, including Somalia. Denmark encourages full and transparent implementation of resolution 2799 (2025) and timely reporting by the Secretary-General.
before.Greece: Thank you, Mr. President. Greece condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks in Palmyra, Bondi Beach and Maiduguri, and extends its condolences to the victims and their families. Greece votes in favour of this resolution. We believe that counter-terrorism must be fully grounded in international law, including international human rights law, international refugee law and international humanitarian law. We underline the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring unimpeded humanitarian access, accountability for all terrorist acts, and implementation of the sanctions regime without politicization or double standards. Greece also supports continued international engagement on Syria and Africa, including capacity-building in affected regions.
before.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder and will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn the terrorist attack in Palmyra and all recent terrorist attacks, including in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri, and extend our condolences to the victims and affected Governments. Guyana supports this text because it reaffirms that counter-terrorism must be conducted in full conformity with international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and because it recognizes the need to protect humanitarian action, civilians, children and survivors. We welcome its emphasis on capacity-building for developing countries, particularly in Africa, and on African-led counter-terrorism efforts, while stressing respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all Member States. Guyana urges full and non-politicized implementation of the resolution and of the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions regime.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. As a country that has suffered immensely from terrorism, including attacks by Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan, we welcome the explicit inclusion of TTP among the terrorist groups that must cease violence, disarm, and prevent recruitment and financing. We also welcome the incorporation of the principle that all Member States must implement their obligations without double standards or politicization. Pakistan supports strengthened international cooperation, capacity-building for developing countries, especially in Africa, and full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States and for international law, including human rights law, refugee law and international humanitarian law. We reiterate that terrorism cannot and should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group, and that counter-terrorism measures must not target any religion or community. Pakistan will continue to support international efforts to combat terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.
before.Panama: Mr. President, Panama thanks the United States for its penholder leadership and will vote in favour of this draft. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Palmyra and all recent terrorist attacks, and we reaffirm that counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full respect for the Charter, international law, human rights, refugee law and humanitarian law. As a maritime nation, Panama especially welcomes the emphasis on border, maritime and port security and on technical assistance and capacity-building for developing countries. We call for full, balanced and non-politicized implementation of the sanctions regime, while ensuring the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian action.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone votes in favour of this resolution. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks in Palmyra, Bondi Beach, Maiduguri and all other recent terrorist attacks. We welcome the Council’s clear message that terrorism cannot and should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group, and that all counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law, including international humanitarian law, international human rights law and international refugee law. For Sierra Leone, the resolution’s attention to Africa is essential. We call for predictable, adequate and sustainable support for African-led counter-terrorism efforts, including through the African Union, ECOWAS, the Multinational Joint Task Force and the Accra Initiative, and for capacity-building in Somalia and across the Sahel, the Lake Chad Basin and the Horn of Africa. We also welcome the focus on accountability for sexual and gender-based violence, the treatment of children associated with terrorist groups as victims, survivors’ access to justice and support, and the need to strengthen efforts against terrorist financing in line with FATF standards. We thank the United States for its penholdership and urge full and even-handed implementation without double standards or politicization.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this resolution. We strongly condemn the terrorist attack in Palmyra and all recent terrorist attacks, and we express our condolences to the victims and their families. We welcome the text’s clear reaffirmation that counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law, including international humanitarian law, human rights law and refugee law, and must not impede impartial humanitarian action or the protection of civilians. We also value the emphasis on accountability for sexual and gender-based violence, the treatment of children associated with terrorist groups primarily as victims, and the need to avoid associating terrorism with any religion or community. Implementation must remain transparent, evidence-based and consistent with the relevant Security Council resolutions, including resolution 2799 (2025). Slovenia will continue to support effective multilateral action against terrorism that upholds the rule of law and the protection of civilians.
before.Somalia: Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the incorporation of our proposed amendment to operative paragraph 8, which now explicitly recognizes the threat posed by Al-Shabaab and the importance of the Horn of Africa, including Somalia. As a country on the front line of terrorism, Somalia supports the Council’s strengthened condemnation of terrorist acts and its call for full implementation of counter-terrorism obligations, while emphasizing that such measures must respect international law, sovereignty and humanitarian action. We particularly value the resolution’s call for enhanced and predictable support for African-led counter-terrorism efforts, including capacity-building for States affected by terrorism, and we urge the Council to ensure that this commitment is translated into concrete action. Somalia remains committed to working with all Member States to prevent the resurgence of ISIL, Al-Qaida, Al-Shabaab and their affiliates, and to addressing the conditions conducive to terrorism across the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and Horn of Africa.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We strongly condemn the terrorist attack in Palmyra and the other recent terrorist attacks, including in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri, and we express our condolences to the victims and their families. This resolution sends a clear and united message that ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida and their affiliates must be defeated, that all States must fully implement their counter-terrorism obligations, and that these efforts must be consistent with international law, including human rights, refugee and humanitarian law. We welcome the resolution’s emphasis on accountability, support for survivors, the protection and reintegration of children, and strengthened support for African-led efforts. We call on the Syrian Arab Republic to honour its commitments under resolution 2799 (2025) and to cooperate fully with the 1267 Committee, and we urge all Member States to prevent the resurgence of terrorism without double standards or politicisation. The United Kingdom remains committed to working with the Council to ensure full implementation.
before.United States of America: The United States strongly supports this resolution and urges its unanimous adoption. This Council must speak with clarity after the despicable ISIL attack in Palmyra that killed American service members and a civilian interpreter, and after other recent terrorist attacks from Australia to Nigeria. The text condemns these attacks, demands that terrorist groups cease violence, strengthens implementation of sanctions and border-security obligations, supports African-led counter-terrorism efforts, and calls on the Syrian Government to uphold its commitments under resolution 2799 (2025). It also rightly safeguards humanitarian action and reaffirms that counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law. The United States will vote in favour.

after.China:
Thank you, Mr. President.

China voted in favour of this resolution. We strongly condemn the terrorist attack in Palmyra, Syria, on 13 December, and all other recent terrorist attacks, including in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri. We extend our condolences to the victims’ families and to the Governments concerned. China supports the Council in sending a united and clear message against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

Counter-terrorism must be comprehensive and cannot be selective or subject to double standards. China calls for resolute action against all terrorist forces, including ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement/Turkistan Islamic Party, Al-Shabaab, Boko Haram, TTP and their affiliates. Afghanistan’s territory must not be used to support or shelter terrorism; we urge the Afghan interim authorities to take credible and effective measures against all terrorist groups.

At the same time, counter-terrorism measures must comply with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, international law and the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all States. They should not be politicized, used as a pretext for interference in internal affairs, or associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group. The implementation of sanctions must be balanced, evidence-based and consistent with the relevant resolutions, and must not impede impartial humanitarian action.

China attaches importance to the situation in Syria. We hope the Syrian authorities will honour their counter-terrorism commitments, prevent the resurgence of terrorist networks, address the threat of foreign terrorist fighters and cooperate with the relevant Security Council mechanisms. The Security Council should continue to handle Syria-related sanctions adjustments in a prudent manner, based on a comprehensive assessment of the counter-terrorism and security situation and the legitimate concerns of all parties. We also support a Syrian-owned and Syrian-led political process.

We support strengthened capacity-building for developing countries, especially in Africa, including through African-led counter-terrorism efforts. China will continue to work with Council members and the wider international community to advance the common cause of counter-terrorism while upholding international law and the central role of the United Nations.
after.France:
Thank you, Mr President. France voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its unanimous adoption. We strongly condemn the terrorist attack in Palmyra on 13 December, which killed two United States service members and a United States civilian interpreter, as well as the attacks in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri and all other recent terrorist attacks. We extend our condolences to the victims’ families and to the Governments and peoples affected.

This text sends a clear message: the fight against ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida and their affiliates remains a priority for the Security Council. That fight is not over. The risk of a resurgence in Syria and Iraq must not be underestimated. France recalls the commitments made by the Syrian authorities under resolution 2799 (2025), in particular to counter terrorism, secure borders and prevent the return of terrorist networks, and calls on them to implement those commitments fully.

France also welcomes the resolution’s reaffirmation that counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full respect for international law, including human rights law, refugee law and international humanitarian law, and must not impede impartial humanitarian action. We welcome the attention given to accountability for sexual and gender-based violence committed by terrorist groups, including against Yazidis, Christians and other minorities, and to the treatment of children associated with terrorist groups primarily as victims. We reiterate that terrorism cannot and should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group.

France will continue to support African-led counter-terrorism efforts and capacity-building, including in the Sahel, the Horn of Africa and the Lake Chad Basin, and will remain fully engaged to ensure that the sanctions regime is implemented rigorously, evidence-based and without politicization.
after.Republic of Korea: Thank you, Mr. President. The Republic of Korea voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its unanimous adoption. We thank the United States for its penholder leadership. We condemn in the strongest terms the ISIL terrorist attack in Palmyra on 13 December and all other recent terrorist attacks, including those in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri, and extend our sincere condolences to the victims’ families and affected Governments. The Republic of Korea remains firmly committed to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. Full and consistent implementation of the relevant Security Council resolutions and the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions regime is essential. At the same time, counter-terrorism measures must be consistent with the Charter and international law, including international human rights law, international refugee law and international humanitarian law, and must not impede impartial humanitarian action. We stress the importance of preventing terrorist financing and the movement of foreign terrorist fighters, strengthening border, maritime, aviation and port security, and enhancing capacity-building for developing countries, especially in Africa and through African-led efforts. We also underscore that terrorism must never be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group, and that the protection of civilians, the treatment of children associated with terrorist groups primarily as victims, and accountability for sexual and gender-based violence must remain central. The Republic of Korea will continue to cooperate actively with the Council and all partners to ensure the full implementation of this resolution.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution just adopted and welcomes its unanimous adoption. This Council has sent a clear, united signal that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations is unacceptable and must be combated resolutely, including the despicable ISIL attack in Palmyra and the other recent terrorist attacks in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri. We express our condolences to the families of the victims and to the affected States.

We supported this text because it reaffirms the central role of the United Nations Charter and the Security Council in counter-terrorism, calls for full implementation of relevant obligations without double standards or politicization, and stresses respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of all States. We also welcome the reaffirmation that counter-terrorism measures must be consistent with international law, including international humanitarian law, and must not impede impartial humanitarian action.

At the same time, we underscore that counter-terrorism must not become a pretext for interference in the internal affairs of States or for unilateral coercive measures. The sanctions regime must be implemented in a balanced, evidence-based and depoliticized manner and must not harm the humanitarian situation or the legitimate socio-economic recovery of affected countries. In the Syrian context, resolution 2799 (2025) was an important step. Any further adjustment of the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions regime related to Syria must be based on an objective assessment of the situation and take into account the legitimate concerns of the Syrian Government and people.

The Russian Federation also supports the resolution’s focus on capacity-building for developing countries, particularly in Africa, and on African-led counter-terrorism efforts. Such assistance must be provided upon request and in full respect for the sovereignty of States. We are convinced that only genuinely collective, non-politicized and law-based cooperation can effectively counter the terrorist threat. The Russian Federation will continue to work constructively within the Security Council to that end.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. It sends a clear and united message that this Council stands against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, and that ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida and their affiliates, including Al-Shabaab, Boko Haram and TTP, must be defeated and held accountable. We reiterate our strongest condemnation of the terrorist attack in Palmyra and all recent terrorist attacks, including in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri, and our condolences to the victims and their families.

The United Kingdom now stresses the importance of full implementation. All Member States must meet their counter-terrorism obligations, including on border security, financing, travel and information-sharing, and they must do so in full compliance with international law, including human rights law, refugee law and international humanitarian law. Counter-terrorism measures must not impede impartial humanitarian action or the protection of civilians. We particularly welcome the resolution’s focus on accountability for sexual and gender-based violence, the treatment of children associated with terrorist groups primarily as victims, and support for survivors. We also welcome the emphasis on strengthened, predictable support for African-led counter-terrorism efforts.

We call on the Syrian Arab Republic to honour the commitments it has made, including under resolution 2799 (2025), to counter terrorism, secure its borders, prevent any resurgence of terrorist networks, and cooperate fully with the relevant Security Council sanctions mechanisms. The United Kingdom will continue to work with all Council members and partners to ensure this resolution is translated into real action that protects the most vulnerable and advances international peace and security.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the Council’s unanimous adoption of this resolution. Today’s vote sends a clear and unified message that this Council stands against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the despicable ISIL attack in Palmyra that killed American service members and a United States civilian interpreter, as well as the recent attacks in Bondi Beach and Maiduguri. We thank all Council members for their constructive engagement. The United States will continue to insist on full and transparent implementation of this text and of the relevant sanctions regime, including through the 1267 Committee and its Monitoring Team. We call on the Syrian Arab Republic to honour its counter-terrorism commitments, including those reflected in resolution 2799 (2025), and on all Member States to implement their obligations without double standards or politicization. We also underscore the importance of supporting African-led counter-terrorism efforts and capacity-building, while ensuring that all counter-terrorism measures comply with international law and do not impede impartial humanitarian action. The Council has spoken with one voice; now we must ensure that this resolution is implemented on the ground.
